```{r}
      table.width = gt::pct(100),

      data_row.padding = gt::px(4),
      column_labels.font.weight = "600",
      source_notes.font.size = gt::px(11)
    )
}
```

## Purpose

This page explains how the verified H02 temporal frames and recorded biological
sex were turned into the inference presented in the
[H11 results report](../../../notebooks/hypotheses/H11.qmd).

H11 asks whether the 24-hour pattern of personal melanopic equivalent daylight
illuminance (melEDI) differs by the biological-sex variable recorded in the
study. Biological sex and gender identity are distinct constructs; gender
identity was not analysed. The near-eye sensor position is primary. The chest
sensor position provides complementary evidence and is not a measure of ocular
exposure. This placement change is recorded in
[`DEV-001`](../../../notebooks/preregistration_deviations.qmd#dev-001).

The reported estimand is the complete Female-minus-Male fitted curve across 48
half-hour clock bins, averaged equally across included sites and conditional on
the fitted temporal, participant, participant-day, site, and autocorrelation
structure. A site-average fitted mean averages across included sites and gives
each site equal weight. The participant is the independent unit for robust
inference. A participant-day is one participant's included observations on one
local calendar day; model rows are 30-minute observations nested within
participant-days and participants.

The accepted preregistration differences are consolidated in the
[H11 preregistration-deviations section](../../../notebooks/hypotheses/H11.qmd#h11-preregistration-deviations).

## Analysis map

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
  A["Verified H02 placement-specific temporal frames"] --> B["Join recorded biological sex"]
  B --> C["Retain 48 local-wall-clock bins and H02 autocorrelation boundaries"]
  C --> D["Fit cyclic sex-pattern model"]
  D --> E["Participant-cluster robust complete-curve test"]
  E --> F["Pointwise 95% curve and contrast intervals"]
  E --> G["Conditional effect-size branch when raw global p < 0.050"]
  D --> H["Two-component level/shape attribution with false-discovery-rate (FDR) adjustment"]
  C --> I["Gap-timing-unaware sensitivity"]
  C --> J["Activity-complete same-sample sensitivity"]
```

## 1. Verified inherited H02 frames

### Frame integrity, schema, keys, and values

All six accepted frames have the required fields, unique participant-day and
clock-bin keys, the complete set of 48 clock positions, non-negative melEDI,
exact response reconstruction as $\log_{10}(\mathrm{melEDI}+0.1)$, matching
biological-sex encodings, and boundary flags consistent with their recorded
reasons. Their file identities and stored sample counts also match.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h11-prep-frame-integrity
#| tbl-cap: "Integrity checks for every accepted H11 frame"

frame_integrity |>
  transmute(
    Analysis = .data$analysis_label,
    `File identity` = .data$file_identity,
    `Schema complete` = if_else(.data$schema_complete, "PASS", "FAIL"),
    `Duplicate keys` = .data$duplicate_row_keys,
    `48-bin grid` = if_else(.data$complete_48_bin_clock_grid, "PASS", "FAIL"),
    `Response error` = .data$response_reconstruction_maximum_absolute_error,
    `AR boundaries` = if_else(
      .data$AR_start_matches_boundary_reason,
      "PASS",
      "FAIL"
    ),
    Overall = .data$overall_status
  ) |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = "Response error", decimals = 3) |>
  prep_gt(font_size = 11)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h11-prep-frame-content
#| tbl-cap: "Frame content and metric-support checks"

frame_integrity |>
  transmute(
    Analysis = .data$analysis_label,
    `Minimum bins/day` = .data$minimum_bins_per_participant_day,
    `Complete participant-days` = .data$complete_48_bin_participant_days,
    `Minimum valid min/bin` = .data$minimum_valid_minutes_per_30_minute_bin,
    `Maximum valid min/bin` = .data$maximum_valid_minutes_per_30_minute_bin,
    `Gap-timing field` = .data$metric_specific_gap_timing_field,
    `Exact zeros` = .data$exact_zero_observations
  ) |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::fmt_integer(columns = c(
    "Minimum bins/day", "Complete participant-days", "Exact zeros"
  )) |>
  prep_gt(font_size = 11)
```

### Temporal and analytical-frame construction

### Inherited time structure

H11 inherits the finalized temporal architecture documented in the
[H02 analysis preparation and provenance](../H02/H02_analysis_preparation.qmd)
rather than selecting a new one. Local wall-clock time is represented by 48
half-hour midpoints from 00:15 to 23:45. The smooth is cyclic, meaning that it
joins smoothly across midnight. Site-specific time patterns sum to zero,
participant-specific time curves represent remaining within-participant
variation, and participant-day random effects represent remaining variation
within local calendar days. The hierarchy and site structure are recorded in
[`DEV-044`](../../../notebooks/preregistration_deviations.qmd#dev-044) and
[`DEV-045`](../../../notebooks/preregistration_deviations.qmd#dev-045).

Autocorrelation sequences are based on true elapsed instants. A sequence
restarts at participant-day boundaries, elapsed-time discontinuities, and
non-one-to-one wall-clock outcomes, including daylight-saving-time ambiguity.
The accepted frames therefore do not infer continuity merely because two rows
have adjacent clock labels.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h11-prep-ar-boundaries-primary
#| tbl-cap: "Autocorrelation-boundary evidence in the primary fitted frames"

AR_boundaries |>
  filter(.data$analysis_label %in% c("Primary near eye", "Complementary chest")) |>
  transmute(
    Analysis = .data$analysis_label,
    `Boundary reason` = .data$boundary_reason,
    Observations = .data$observations,
    `Share of frame` = .data$percent_of_frame / 100
  ) |>
  gt::gt(groupname_col = "Analysis") |>
  gt::fmt_integer(columns = "Observations") |>
  gt::fmt_percent(columns = "Share of frame", decimals = 2) |>
  prep_gt(font_size = 11)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h11-prep-ar-boundaries-sensitivity
#| tbl-cap: "Autocorrelation-boundary evidence in the sensitivity frames"

AR_boundaries |>
  filter(!.data$analysis_label %in% c("Primary near eye", "Complementary chest")) |>
  transmute(
    Analysis = .data$analysis_label,
    `Boundary reason` = .data$boundary_reason,
    Observations = .data$observations,
    `Share of frame` = .data$percent_of_frame / 100
  ) |>
  gt::gt(groupname_col = "Analysis") |>
  gt::fmt_integer(columns = "Observations") |>
  gt::fmt_percent(columns = "Share of frame", decimals = 2) |>
  prep_gt(font_size = 11)
```

### Coverage, missingness, and transformation

The general data-admission rules required at least 50% valid data per hour and
at least 80% valid data per participant-day. The primary model frames then
required 15–30 valid wall-clock minutes in each retained 30-minute melEDI bin.
The participant-day inclusion differences are recorded in
[`DEV-019`](../../../notebooks/preregistration_deviations.qmd#dev-019) and
[`DEV-057`](../../../notebooks/preregistration_deviations.qmd#dev-057).

All non-negative melEDI values, including exact zeros, are retained. The model
response is $\log_{10}(\mathrm{melEDI}+0.1)$, so zero maps exactly to -1 on the
model scale. The descriptive figure uses a symlog display scale that is linear
from 0 to 1 lx and base-10 logarithmic above 1 lx, with labels in original
units. It shows the retained zeros separately.
The accepted 30-minute outcome and transformation are recorded in
[`DEV-042`](../../../notebooks/preregistration_deviations.qmd#dev-042).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h11-prep-samples
#| tbl-cap: "Exact analytical samples"

sample_support |>
  transmute(
    Analysis = .data$analysis_label,
    Participants = .data$participants,
    `Female / Male` = paste0(
      .data$female_participants,
      " / ",
      .data$male_participants
    ),
    `Participant-days` = .data$participant_days,
    `30-min observations` = .data$observations_30_minute,
    `Nominal hours` = .data$nominal_observation_hours,
    Sites = .data$sites,
    `AR sequences` = .data$AR_sequences
  ) |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::fmt_integer(columns = c(
    "Participants", "Participant-days", "30-min observations", "Sites",
    "AR sequences"
  )) |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = "Nominal hours", decimals = 1, use_seps = TRUE) |>
  prep_gt(font_size = 11)
```

The primary near-eye model uses **141 participants, 816 participant-days,
37,756 observations (18,878.0 nominal hours), and 9 sites**. The complementary
chest model uses **154 participants, 902 participant-days, 41,842 observations
(20,921.0 nominal hours), and 8 sites**. These counts reconcile exactly with
the accepted H02 fitted samples. Retained samples include documented
participants outside the preregistered age or employment criteria. Comparable
exclusion-sensitivity coverage is not uniform across all affected hypotheses,
as recorded in
[`DEV-003`](../../../notebooks/preregistration_deviations.qmd#dev-003).

## 2. Nonlinear GAM construction

A nonlinear generalized additive model (GAM) allows the daily melEDI pattern
to vary smoothly and nonlinearly over clock time. Cyclic smooths join smoothly
across midnight. Participant-specific time curves and participant-day random
effects represent remaining repeated-measure variation after the shared time,
biological-sex, and site structure is considered. Autocorrelation is residual
similarity between observations close together in time; an AR(1) structure
represents this similarity as stronger at shorter lags.

### Exact Wilkinson formulas

The following are the exact formulas supplied to the accepted model fits. The
cells are displayed for auditability and are not executed on this page.

```{r}
#| label: h11-exact-pattern-formula
#| eval: false

M_pattern <- response ~ sex +
  s(time_hour, bs = "cc", k = 12) +
  s(time_hour, by = sex_smooth, bs = "cc", k = 12) +
  s(time_hour, site, bs = "sz", k = 12) +
  s(time_hour, participant, bs = "fs", k = 10) +
  s(participant_day, bs = "re")
```

```{r}
#| label: h11-exact-effect-baseline-formula
#| eval: false

M_0 <- response ~
  s(time_hour, bs = "cc", k = 12) +
  s(time_hour, site, bs = "sz", k = 12) +
  s(time_hour, participant, bs = "fs", k = 10) +
  s(participant_day, bs = "re")
```

```{r}
#| label: h11-exact-activity-formula
#| eval: false

M_activity <- response ~ sex + activity +
  s(time_hour, bs = "cc", k = 12) +
  s(time_hour, by = sex_smooth, bs = "cc", k = 12) +
  s(time_hour, by = activity_smooth, bs = "cc", k = 12, id = 2) +
  s(time_hour, site, bs = "sz", k = 12) +
  s(time_hour, participant, bs = "fs", k = 10) +
  s(participant_day, bs = "re")
```

```{r}
#| label: h11-exact-activity-effect-baseline-formula
#| eval: false

M_activity_0 <- response ~ activity +
  s(time_hour, bs = "cc", k = 12) +
  s(time_hour, by = activity_smooth, bs = "cc", k = 12, id = 2) +
  s(time_hour, site, bs = "sz", k = 12) +
  s(time_hour, participant, bs = "fs", k = 10) +
  s(participant_day, bs = "re")
```

The sex factor uses Male as the treatment-reference level. The ordered
`sex_smooth` factor identifies the cyclic Female-minus-Male deviation. The
main cyclic smooth is the Male reference curve; the sex-deviation smooth adds
the Female shape difference. Site deviations use the sum-to-zero basis,
participant curves use factor smooths, and participant-day random intercepts
account for repeated observations within days. In the activity model, Home is
the treatment reference and the ordered activity deviation smooths share one
smoothing parameter (`id = 2`).

The biological-sex/time specification is recorded in
[`DEV-043`](../../../notebooks/preregistration_deviations.qmd#dev-043), and the
site and participant structure is recorded in
[`DEV-044`](../../../notebooks/preregistration_deviations.qmd#dev-044) and
[`DEV-045`](../../../notebooks/preregistration_deviations.qmd#dev-045).

## 3. Estimand, uncertainty, and multiplicity

### Complete-curve inference

The complete-curve, or global, test is one joint test of the time-constant and
time-varying Female-minus-Male contributions across the whole 48-bin, 24-hour
curve within each placement and dataset. Inference
uses participant-summed, AR-whitened scores; a participant-cluster CR1
covariance; the smoothing-bias term $V_p-V_e$; and a finite-cluster,
fractional-rank $F$ reference. A pointwise 95% confidence interval (95% CI)
applies to one displayed clock bin. It is not a simultaneous band across the
full day. All displayed curve, contrast, and scalar intervals are pointwise 95%
CIs.

The primary near-eye global raw p-value is
`r format_p(near_global$p_raw)` and the complementary chest raw p-value is
`r format_p(chest_global$p_raw)`. Each is the sole member of its explicitly
labelled global family, so its stored adjusted value is numerically identical.
FDR adjustment is applied within separately labelled families. This
complete-curve inference and multiplicity specification is
recorded in
[`DEV-048`](../../../notebooks/preregistration_deviations.qmd#dev-048).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h11-prep-global-tests
#| tbl-cap: "Complete-curve tests; raw and FDR-adjusted p-values are labelled and styled independently"

global_display <- global_tests |>
  mutate(
    raw_significant = .data$p_raw < 0.05,
    adjusted_significant = .data$p_adjusted < 0.05,
    `Raw p` = format_p(.data$p_raw),
    `FDR-adjusted p` = format_p(.data$p_adjusted)
  ) |>
  transmute(
    Dataset = .data$dataset_label,
    Placement = .data$placement_label,
    `F statistic` = .data$F_statistic,
    `Numerator df` = .data$fractional_numerator_df,
    `Denominator df` = .data$denominator_df,
    `Raw p`,
    `FDR-adjusted p`,
    `Family size` = .data$observed_family_n,
    Decision = if_else(.data$adjusted_significant, "Supported", "Not supported"),
    raw_significant,
    adjusted_significant
  )

global_display |>
  gt::gt(groupname_col = "Dataset") |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = c("F statistic", "Numerator df"), decimals = 3) |>
  gt::fmt_integer(columns = c("Denominator df", "Family size")) |>
  gt::tab_style(
    style = gt::cell_text(weight = "bold"),
    locations = gt::cells_body(columns = "Raw p", rows = raw_significant)
  ) |>
  gt::tab_style(
    style = gt::cell_text(weight = "bold"),
    locations = gt::cells_body(columns = "FDR-adjusted p", rows = adjusted_significant)
  ) |>
  gt::cols_hide(columns = c("raw_significant", "adjusted_significant")) |>
  prep_gt(font_size = 11) |>
  gt::tab_source_note(
    gt::md("Significance rule: each labelled global family has one test; $p<0.050$.")
  )
```

### What the two-component decomposition can and cannot say

The complete-curve result is the overall test. A separate, secondary
decomposition asks whether that curve difference can be attributed cleanly to
(1) a constant parametric level component or (2) a cyclic shape component.
Those two attribution tests form a two-test FDR family within each placement
and dataset.

No component remains supported after that two-test adjustment. This does
**not** invalidate or reverse the significant global curve result. It means
only that the evidence cannot cleanly separate the overall curve association
into an independent “level” contribution and an independent “shape”
contribution after accounting for the two attribution attempts. The two
components are parameterization-dependent parts of one fitted curve and are
not a second omnibus test of whether the full curve differs.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h11-prep-decomposition
#| tbl-cap: "Secondary level/shape attribution tests with within-run two-test FDR adjustment"

decomposition_display <- decomposition |>
  mutate(
    raw_significant = .data$p_raw < 0.05,
    adjusted_significant = .data$p_adjusted < 0.05,
    `Raw p` = format_p(.data$p_raw),
    `FDR-adjusted p` = format_p(.data$p_adjusted)
  ) |>
  transmute(
    Dataset = .data$dataset_label,
    Placement = .data$placement_label,
    Component = recode(
      .data$comparison_id,
      parametric_level_component = "Level",
      cyclic_shape_component = "Shape"
    ),
    `F statistic` = .data$F_statistic,
    `Numerator df` = .data$fractional_numerator_df,
    `Raw p`,
    `FDR-adjusted p`,
    Decision = if_else(
      .data$adjusted_significant,
      "Attribution supported",
      "Attribution not resolved"
    ),
    raw_significant,
    adjusted_significant
  )

decomposition_display |>
  gt::gt(groupname_col = "Dataset") |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = c("F statistic", "Numerator df"), decimals = 3) |>
  gt::tab_style(
    style = gt::cell_text(weight = "bold"),
    locations = gt::cells_body(columns = "Raw p", rows = raw_significant)
  ) |>
  gt::tab_style(
    style = gt::cell_text(weight = "bold"),
    locations = gt::cells_body(
      columns = "FDR-adjusted p",
      rows = adjusted_significant
    )
  ) |>
  gt::cols_hide(columns = c("raw_significant", "adjusted_significant")) |>
  prep_gt(font_size = 11) |>
  gt::tab_source_note(
    gt::md("Significance rule: FDR-adjusted $p<0.050$ within each two-component attribution family.")
  )
```

### Conditional effect-size branch

The predeclared effect-size branch opens only when the placement-specific raw
global test has $p<0.050$. It opened for both primary placements. The reported
curve-variation estimator is the mean, across 48 clock bins, of the sample
variance across the two equally weighted fitted biological-sex curves. It is a
conditional descriptive magnitude on the squared model-prediction scale, not
variance explained. Its 95% interval uses the accepted participant-cluster
robust covariance and first-order delta method.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h11-prep-effect-sizes
#| tbl-cap: "Conditional descriptive effect-size estimates for globally supported primary curves"

curve_effects |>
  transmute(
    Placement = .data$placement_label,
    Participants = .data$participants,
    `Participant-days` = .data$participant_days,
    Observations = .data$observations_30_minute,
    Estimate = .data$estimate,
    `Lower 95%` = .data$lower_95,
    `Upper 95%` = .data$upper_95,
    Unit = .data$unit
  ) |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::fmt_integer(columns = c("Participants", "Participant-days", "Observations")) |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = c("Estimate", "Lower 95%", "Upper 95%"), decimals = 4) |>
  prep_gt(font_size = 11)
```

The fitted parametric level coefficient is also reported with its
participant-cluster-robust pointwise 95% CI, but its interpretation is
conditional on the cyclic sex-deviation smooth and must not be used as a
stand-alone replacement for the complete-curve test. For the shifted-value
ratio, both fitted values are shifted by the model's 0.1-lx offset before the
Female-to-Male ratio is calculated.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h11-prep-parametric-level
#| tbl-cap: "Conditional parametric level estimates in the primary fits"

parametric_levels |>
  transmute(
    Placement = .data$placement_label,
    `Female-minus-Male estimate` = .data$estimate_eta,
    `Lower 95%` = .data$lower_eta_95,
    `Upper 95%` = .data$upper_eta_95,
    `Shifted-value ratio` = .data$female_to_male_shifted_ratio,
    `Ratio lower 95%` = .data$ratio_lower_95,
    `Ratio upper 95%` = .data$ratio_upper_95
  ) |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = 2:7, decimals = 3) |>
  prep_gt()
```

## 4. Model checks, residual dependence, and influence

The model checks (model diagnostics) covered convergence and warnings, cyclic closure at
midnight, site sum-to-zero constraints, basis dimensions, residual
distributions, boundary-aware residual autocorrelation, formal concurvity,
robust covariance behaviour, participant influence, and agreement between the
curve-space and coefficient-block formulations of the global test.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h11-prep-diagnostic-assessment
#| tbl-cap: "Overall diagnostic assessment for primary and gap-timing-unaware fits"

diagnostics |>
  transmute(
    Dataset = .data$dataset_label,
    Placement = .data$placement_label,
    Assessment = .data$classification,
    Converged = .data$converged,
    `Cyclic closure` = .data$cyclic_sex_curves_close_at_midnight,
    `Site constraint` = .data$site_sum_to_zero_verified,
    `Final lag-1 residual correlation` =
      .data$final_boundary_aware_lag1_correlation,
    `Severe basis flags` = .data$severe_k_check_flags
  ) |>
  gt::gt(groupname_col = "Dataset") |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = "Final lag-1 residual correlation", decimals = 3) |>
  gt::fmt_integer(columns = "Severe basis flags") |>
  prep_gt(font_size = 11)
```

All four models were assessed as **acceptable with specified limitations**.
They converged without serious warnings, closed cyclically at midnight,
preserved the inherited site constraint, had no severe basis-dimension flags,
and reduced boundary-aware lag-1 residual correlation to 0.070–0.083. The
remaining limitations are the Gaussian log-scale mean assumption, exact-zero
mass, heavy residual tails, heteroscedasticity, and concurvity inherited from
the H02 temporal analysis. These caution against interpreting the curves as a
complete generative account of melEDI, but they did not trigger the prespecified
unacceptable-model criteria.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h11-prep-robust-influence
#| tbl-cap: "Participant-cluster robust covariance and delete-one-participant stability"

robust_diagnostics |>
  transmute(
    Dataset = .data$dataset_label,
    Placement = .data$placement_label,
    Participants = .data$participants,
    `Maximum cluster score share` =
      .data$maximum_participant_unscaled_meat_share,
    `Effective clusters` = .data$effective_participants_unscaled_meat_trace,
    `Delete-one p minimum` = format_p(.data$delete_one_participant_p_minimum),
    `Delete-one p median` = format_p(.data$delete_one_participant_p_median),
    `Delete-one p maximum` = format_p(.data$delete_one_participant_p_maximum),
    `Delete-one results below 0.050` =
      .data$delete_one_participant_below_0_05
  ) |>
  gt::gt(groupname_col = "Dataset") |>
  gt::fmt_integer(columns = c("Participants", "Delete-one results below 0.050")) |>
  gt::fmt_number(
    columns = c("Maximum cluster score share", "Effective clusters"),
    decimals = 3
  ) |>
  prep_gt(font_size = 11) |>
  gt::tab_source_note(
    gt::md("The displayed delete-one p-values are raw global-test values; no new multiplicity family is created by this influence screen.")
  )
```

Every delete-one-participant primary and sensitivity result remained below
0.050. Maximum participant score contribution ranged from 2.7% to 7.6%, while
the effective number of contributing clusters was smaller than the nominal
participant count, especially for chest. The robust covariance therefore
materially protects inference from within-participant dependence, but the
chest result should still be read as complementary.

Results remain conditional on the observed sites, and the site count is too
small for broad site-population generalisation. Leave-one-site-out refits have
not been completed, so site influence beyond the recorded checks remains an
explicit unresolved limitation.

## 5. Sensitivity analyses and deferred comparisons

### Gap timing

The **gap-timing-unaware dataset** still passed the general requirement for at
least 50% valid data per hour and at least 80% valid data per participant-day.
“Gap-timing-unaware” means that the timing of the remaining missing
observations is not used for metric-specific adjustment. For contrast only in
this first explanation, the primary dataset could be interpreted as a
**time-sensitive primary metric dataset**; hereafter it is called simply the
primary dataset.

Applying the same model and global test to the gap-timing-unaware dataset gave
raw global p-values of
`r format_p(global_tests$p_raw[global_tests$dataset_label == "Gap-timing-unaware dataset" & global_tests$placement_label == "Near eye"])`
near eye and
`r format_p(global_tests$p_raw[global_tests$dataset_label == "Gap-timing-unaware dataset" & global_tests$placement_label == "Chest"])`
at chest. This supports stability to whether the timing of remaining missing
observations is used for metric-specific adjustment. It does not test every
possible missing-data mechanism.

### Activity context

The exploratory activity analysis uses the accepted primary placement frames
and a normalized hourly diary. A 30-minute observation is retained only when
there is exactly one containing diary hour and exactly one eligible mapped
activity: Home, Sleep, Public transport/car, Indoor work/home office, or
Outdoors/active travel. Missing flags, no selection, multiple selections, and
an unspecified “other” selection are not imputed. Autocorrelation sequences
restart across gaps created by this filter.

```{r}
#| label: fig-h11-prep-activity-attrition
#| fig-cap: "Observation-level activity matching and attrition from each accepted placement-specific frame. Paired horizontal bars use a common 0–100% axis and carry direct percentage labels; classifications sum to 100% within each placement."
#| fig-alt: "Grouped horizontal bar chart comparing near-eye and chest percentages for six activity-matching outcomes. About four-fifths of near-eye observations and almost nine-tenths of chest observations had one eligible mapped activity. The largest exclusion category is missing activity flags, with smaller shares for unmatched hours, no activity, multiple activities, and unspecified other activity."
#| out-width: "100%"

knitr::include_graphics(file.path(
  root,
  "artifacts/10_figures/H11/preparation/H11_preparation_activity_attrition.png"
))
```

[Paired activity-attrition source data](../../../artifacts/11_source_data/H11/preparation/H11_preparation_activity_attrition.csv)

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h11-prep-activity-attrition
#| tbl-cap: "Activity matching and observation-level attrition"

activity_attrition |>
  transmute(
    Placement = .data$placement_label,
    Classification = .data$status_label,
    `30-min observations` = .data$observations_30_minute,
    `Share of accepted frame` = .data$percent_of_original_frame / 100
  ) |>
  arrange(.data$Classification, .data$Placement) |>
  gt::gt(groupname_col = "Classification") |>
  gt::fmt_integer(columns = "30-min observations") |>
  gt::fmt_percent(columns = "Share of accepted frame", decimals = 1) |>
  prep_gt(font_size = 11)
```

This creates same-sample near-eye models with 126 participants, 724
participant-days, and 30,499 observations, and chest models with 150
participants, 875 participant-days, and 36,711 observations. The comparison
between models with and without activity is descriptive contextualization; it
cannot show that activity mediates or causes a biological-sex association. The
exploratory context is recorded in
[`DEV-047`](../../../notebooks/preregistration_deviations.qmd#dev-047).

The activity comparison separates sample restriction from covariate
adjustment. First, the unadjusted sex-pattern model is refitted to the exact
activity-complete sample. Second, activity level and activity-specific cyclic
deviations are added on that same sample. Because both models use identical
rows, the difference is not confounded by the activity-related attrition
between those two fits.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h11-prep-activity-global
#| tbl-cap: "Exploratory same-sample activity contextualization of the complete sex-curve test"

activity_display <- activity_comparison |>
  mutate(
    raw_significant = .data$p_raw < 0.05,
    adjusted_significant = .data$p_adjusted < 0.05,
    `Raw p` = format_p(.data$p_raw),
    `FDR-adjusted p` = format_p(.data$p_adjusted)
  ) |>
  transmute(
    Placement = .data$placement_label,
    Analysis = .data$analysis_step,
    Participants = .data$participants,
    `Participant-days` = .data$participant_days,
    Observations = .data$observations_30_minute,
    `F statistic` = .data$F_statistic,
    `Raw p`,
    `FDR-adjusted p`,
    Decision = if_else(.data$adjusted_significant, "Supported", "Not supported"),
    raw_significant,
    adjusted_significant
  )

activity_display |>
  gt::gt(groupname_col = "Placement") |>
  gt::fmt_integer(columns = c("Participants", "Participant-days", "Observations")) |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = "F statistic", decimals = 3) |>
  gt::tab_style(
    style = gt::cell_text(weight = "bold"),
    locations = gt::cells_body(columns = "Raw p", rows = raw_significant)
  ) |>
  gt::tab_style(
    style = gt::cell_text(weight = "bold"),
    locations = gt::cells_body(columns = "FDR-adjusted p", rows = adjusted_significant)
  ) |>
  gt::cols_hide(columns = c("raw_significant", "adjusted_significant")) |>
  prep_gt(font_size = 11) |>
  gt::tab_source_note(
    gt::md("Each row is an explicitly labelled one-test exploratory global family; $p<0.050$. Activity-adjusted inference is contextual, not causal or mediational.")
  )
```

On the activity-complete near-eye sample, the unadjusted raw p-value was
`r format_p(activity_comparison$p_raw[activity_comparison$placement_label == "Near eye" & activity_comparison$analysis_step == "Activity-complete sample, unadjusted"])`
and the activity-adjusted raw p-value was
`r format_p(activity_comparison$p_raw[activity_comparison$placement_label == "Near eye" & activity_comparison$analysis_step == "Same sample, activity-adjusted"])`.
At chest these were
`r format_p(activity_comparison$p_raw[activity_comparison$placement_label == "Chest" & activity_comparison$analysis_step == "Activity-complete sample, unadjusted"])`
and
`r format_p(activity_comparison$p_raw[activity_comparison$placement_label == "Chest" & activity_comparison$analysis_step == "Same sample, activity-adjusted"])`.
Thus the activity-adjusted exploratory global tests do not meet the 0.050
rule. This is compatible with attenuation or reduced precision, but it does
not establish that activity explains, mediates, or makes the accepted primary
association disappear.

The root-mean-square (RMS) contrast summarizes the typical absolute size of the
Female-minus-Male curve difference across the 48 clock bins.

```{r}

activity_attenuation |>

      .data$maximum_absolute_cross_model_change_eta,

    )

    decimals = 3

  gt::fmt_percent(columns = "Relative RMS change", decimals = 1) |>
  prep_gt(font_size = 11)
```

No activity-adjusted effect-size estimate is reported because both
activity-adjusted raw global p-values were at or above 0.050. This follows the


### Placement comparability and analyses not run

A scalar near-eye-versus-chest identity plot is not valid for H11. The stored
primary fits use different all-available samples, and H11 has no fitted
common-sample placement outputs or prespecified scalar reduction of its
temporal estimand. The reader report therefore presents separate near-eye and
chest curves without implying equivalence or a paired placement difference.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h11-prep-placement-assessment
#| tbl-cap: "Assessment of a paired near-eye-versus-chest display"

paired_assessment |>
  transmute(

      .data$stored_common_sample_participants,

      .data$stored_common_sample_participant_days,
```

The registered hourly geometric-mean specification remains preregistration

## 6. Technical provenance

::: {.callout-note title="What this page executes"}
When rendered, this page recalculates only file-identity, schema, key, and
lightweight descriptive checks from accepted analysis frames. It reads model
specifications, fitted summaries, estimates, intervals, model checks,
influence screens, and sensitivity outputs from recorded files. It does not
fit or refit a model, estimate autocorrelation, calculate predictions, rerun
resampling, or repeat robust inference.
:::

### Consequential input identities

Ten consequential inputs were checked against the identities recorded when
the analysis frames were accepted. They include the signed preregistration,
the extracted H11 contract, the finalized H02 temporal specification,
biological-sex metadata, the site display registry, four placement/scenario
frames, and the normalized activity diary.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h11-prep-input-identities
#| tbl-cap: "Consequential input identities checked against their recorded SHA-256 values"

input_identities |>
  transmute(
    Input = .data$input,
    `Recorded SHA-256` = substr(.data$expected_sha256, 1, 12),
    `Current SHA-256` = substr(.data$current_sha256, 1, 12),
    Status = .data$verification
  ) |>
  gt::gt() |>
  prep_gt() |>
  gt::tab_style(
    style = gt::cell_text(weight = "bold", color = "#117733"),
    locations = gt::cells_body(columns = "Status", rows = Status == "PASS")
  ) |>
  gt::tab_source_note(
    gt::md("Full 64-character hashes remain in the paired source CSV.")
  )
```

### Recorded formula registry and engine settings

The table below retains fit-role and gate labels for technical reproducibility.
They are not additional scientific results.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h11-prep-formula-registry
#| tbl-cap: "Recorded formula roles and fit gates"

bind_rows(
  formula_manifest |>
    distinct(.data$formula_id, .data$formula, .data$fit_role) |>
    filter(.data$formula_id %in% c("proposed_mpattern", "proposed_m0")) |>
    transmute(
      Model = recode(
        .data$formula_id,
        proposed_mpattern = "Sex-pattern model",
        proposed_m0 = "Conditional effect-size baseline"
      ),
      Role = .data$fit_role,
      Formula = .data$formula
    ),
  activity_formula_manifest |>
    filter(.data$formula_id %in% c("activity_adjusted", "activity_adjusted_no_sex")) |>
    transmute(
      Model = recode(
        .data$formula_id,
        activity_adjusted = "Activity-adjusted sex-pattern model",
        activity_adjusted_no_sex = "Activity-adjusted effect-size baseline"
      ),
      Role = paste(.data$fit_role, "Fit rule:", .data$fit_gate),
      Formula = .data$formula
    )
) |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::cols_width(Model ~ gt::px(190), Role ~ gt::px(260), Formula ~ gt::px(700)) |>
  prep_gt(font_size = 10)
```

All models are Gaussian identity-link additive models fitted by fast REML with
`discrete = TRUE` and cyclic knots `time_hour = c(0, 24)`. For each run, a
preliminary full model with $\rho=0$ estimates the lag-1 residual correlation
within the inherited `AR_start` sequences. The final full model uses that one
run-specific $\rho$. Any conditional effect-size baseline uses the same frame,
$\rho$, knots, and non-sex structure.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h11-prep-fit-settings
#| tbl-cap: "Accepted final-model settings and run-specific autocorrelation"

bind_rows(
  fit_summary |>
    filter(.data$model_id == "mpattern_final_fREML") |>
    transmute(
      Analysis = case_when(
        .data$data_scenario_id == "main" & .data$placement == "glasses" ~
          "Primary near eye",
        .data$data_scenario_id == "main" & .data$placement == "chest" ~
          "Complementary chest",
        .data$data_scenario_id != "main" & .data$placement == "glasses" ~
          "Gap-timing-unaware near eye",
        TRUE ~ "Gap-timing-unaware chest"
      ),
      Observations = .data$n,
      `Total edf` = .data$total_edf,
      Rho = .data$rho,
      Converged = .data$convergence,
      `Elapsed seconds` = .data$elapsed_seconds,
      Engine = paste0("mgcv ", .data$mgcv_version, "; fREML; discrete")
    ),
  activity_fit_summary |>
    filter(.data$model_variant == "activity_adjusted") |>
    transmute(
      Analysis = if_else(
        .data$placement == "glasses",
        "Activity-adjusted near eye",
        "Activity-adjusted chest"
      ),
      Observations = .data$n,
      `Total edf` = .data$total_edf,
      Rho = .data$rho,
      Converged = .data$convergence,
      `Elapsed seconds` = .data$elapsed_seconds,
      Engine = paste0("mgcv ", .data$mgcv_version, "; fREML; discrete")
    )
) |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::fmt_integer(columns = "Observations") |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = c("Total edf", "Rho", "Elapsed seconds"), decimals = 3) |>
  prep_gt(font_size = 11)
```

### Code map and execution order

The scientific computation was separated into bounded, checkpointed steps so
that each fitted object and downstream calculation has a recorded input
identity. This page itself executes only the final display step.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h11-prep-code-map
#| tbl-cap: "H11 computational and reporting code map"

tibble::tribble(
  ~Order, ~Purpose, ~Entry_point,
  1L, "Construct and verify accepted frames", "scripts/hypotheses/H11/build_h11_stage2_frames.R",
  2L, "Fit preliminary and final temporal models", "scripts/hypotheses/H11/run_h11_stage2_models.R",
  3L, "Construct participant-cluster robust tests", "scripts/hypotheses/H11/run_h11_stage2_robust_inference.R",
  4L, "Calculate gated primary effect-size summaries", "scripts/hypotheses/H11/run_h11_stage2_effect_size_pilot.R",
  5L, "Build and analyse activity-complete frames", "scripts/hypotheses/H11/run_h11_activity_context.R",
  6L, "Create reader tables, figures, and source data", "scripts/hypotheses/H11/build_h11_stage3_artifacts.R",
  7L, "Create preparation-only checks and displays", "scripts/hypotheses/H11/build_h11_preparation_artifacts.R",
  8L, "Render this bounded provenance page", "audit/hypotheses/H11/H11_analysis_preparation.qmd"
) |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::cols_width(Purpose ~ gt::px(380), Entry_point ~ gt::px(600)) |>
  prep_gt(font_size = 10)
```

### Output and claim provenance

Every claim in the result report can be traced to a full-precision stored
table or figure source. The preparation figures also have paired CSVs and
physical-size QA records. Internal filenames preserve computational
traceability even where reader-facing terminology has been updated.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h11-prep-output-map
#| tbl-cap: "Principal H11 outputs and the claims they support"

tibble::tribble(
  ~Claim_or_display, ~Authoritative_output,
  "Exact fitted samples", "artifacts/09_tables/H11/stage3/H11_reader_samples.csv",
  "Complete-curve tests", "artifacts/09_tables/H11/stage3/H11_reader_global_tests.csv",
  "Level/shape attribution", "artifacts/09_tables/H11/stage3/H11_reader_level_shape_decomposition.csv",
  "Pointwise curves and contrasts", "artifacts/11_source_data/H11/stage3/H11_reader_sex_specific_curves.csv and H11_reader_female_minus_male_contrasts.csv",
  "Conditional effect sizes", "artifacts/09_tables/H11/stage3/H11_reader_curve_variation_effect_size.csv",
  "Activity contextualization", "artifacts/09_tables/H11/stage3/H11_reader_activity_global_comparison.csv",
  "Primary diagnostics", "artifacts/08_diagnostics/H11/stage3/H11_reader_diagnostic_assessment.csv",
  "Robust influence checks", "artifacts/08_diagnostics/H11/stage3/H11_reader_robust_diagnostics.csv",
  "Figure physical-size QA", "artifacts/12_manifests/H11/H11_stage3_figure_readability_qa.csv",
  "Preparation-page physical-size QA", "artifacts/12_manifests/H11/H11_preparation_figure_readability_qa.csv"
) |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::cols_width(Claim_or_display ~ gt::px(310), Authoritative_output ~ gt::px(760)) |>
  prep_gt(font_size = 10)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h11-prep-figure-qa
#| tbl-cap: "Physical-size readability verification for preparation figures"

qa |>
  transmute(
    Figure = .data$figure_id,
    `Native width (mm)` = .data$native_export_width_mm,
    `Intended width (mm)` = .data$intended_display_width_mm,
    `Scale factor` = .data$display_reduction_factor,
    `Smallest essential nominal text (pt)` =
      .data$smallest_essential_nominal_text_pt,
    `Effective essential text (pt)` =
      .data$effective_final_essential_text_pt,
    `Effective minor text (pt)` = .data$effective_final_minor_text_pt,
    Status = .data$overall_status
  ) |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::fmt_number(
    columns = c(
      "Native width (mm)", "Intended width (mm)", "Scale factor",
      "Smallest essential nominal text (pt)",
      "Effective essential text (pt)", "Effective minor text (pt)"
    ),
    decimals = 2
  ) |>
  prep_gt(font_size = 11)
```

### How to examine or reproduce H11

Use the project R 4.6.1 library and run only the H11 entry points in their
recorded order. The frozen fitted outputs and source-data files allow the
reader report and this preparation record to be rendered without repeating
model fits or resampling. Rebuilding scientific artifacts should occur only
when an analytical input or approved method changes, and should then produce
new hashes and manifests rather than silently replacing accepted evidence.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h11-prep-environment
#| tbl-cap: "Recorded computational environment for preparation verification"

environment |>
  transmute(Component = .data$component, Version = .data$version, Role = .data$role) |>
  gt::gt() |>
  prep_gt()
```

The preparation-report manifest records every H11-scoped script, test,
scientific artifact, source-data CSV, figure, report source, rendered report,
and consequential shared policy file with SHA-256, byte size, producer, and R
version. Its own integrity is checked after rendering so that the manifest
does not contain a circular self-hash.
